kitDescription: Milk: Blooming Bunny is an Iron-element sniper Attacker whose Burst III is a pure self-buff package: for 10 seconds after she casts it she gains +220% ATK and +117.64% Pierce Damage, and while that 'Overconfident, Huh?!' state is up she also hits every enemy for 447.7% of her final ATK as Distributed Damage every 2 seconds (5 hits per burst window). Her Skill 1 grants her the Pierce damage type for 6 seconds on every full-charge attack, which is what makes those Pierce Damage buffs actually do anything. Skill 1's second half is the 'Embarrassment' state: if she holds a completed full charge for half a second while not already embarrassed, she deals a 290% Distributed hit, dumps her entire magazine, force-reloads at half reload speed, and gains +118.7% ATK for 40 seconds. Skill 2 adds +64.7% Pierce Damage for as long as she stays embarrassed. Her burst also makes her immune to Embarrassment for its 10 seconds, so the two states never overlap — and because the state needs a deliberately HELD charge, it is a manual-play combo the auto AI does not perform.

redAssertions: skill1 e1 'rider fires at a GATED cadence': riderHits(BASE) - riderHits(NO_290) == 0 — the 290% block is mode-gated to manual, so it never fires on the default auto basis
skill1 e2/e4 'ammo removal modeled': driver encodes the dump as a passive maxAmmoPct -100, not consumeAmmo — P_NO_AMMO.touched == 0 and effectsOfSlot(skill1, consumeAmmo).length == 0
skill1 e5 'ATK 118.7% for 40 sec, self only': no buffApply(atkPct,118.7) in auto; authored effect also carries no durationSec (permanent-in-manual approximation)
skill1 e5 'the 40 sec window is real': BASE.total == NO_EMB_ATK.total == EMB_ATK_10.total in auto
skill2 'Pierce Damage 64.7% applied to milk only': no such buffApply — the line is deliberately unmodeled
skill2 'Pierce Damage 64.7% is continuous': no authored pierceDamagePct 64.7 effect
skill2 '447.7% rider is a 2 sec cadence...': eff.flavor === 'distributed' fails — the driver's dot carries no flavor field
burst 'Pierce 117.64 removal cannot RAISE damage': P_NO_PIERCE_BUFF.touched >= 2 fails (only one pierceDamagePct buff authored, since 64.7 is unmodeled)

skill1.kitLine: Full Charge attack → Gain Pierce 6 sec
skill1.driverSaid: shotFired → gainPierce durationSec 6, self, active in BOTH modes
skill1.blindSaid: S5: same (asserts timed gainPierce, NOT static hasPierce) — PASS. S6: identical encoding, same shotFired keying and same rationale
skill1.formulaCheck: damage-calculation §1e / mechanics §11: Pierce Damage ▲ is a DamageUp-bucket term that only pays out on Pierce-tagged shots; the timed gainPierce window (pierceUntilFrame) is the sanctioned primitive, and hasPierce:true would wrongly tag her from t=0. SR auto always full-charges (mechanics §4/§7), so shotFired == full-charge attack for her.
skill1.explanation: Fires every shot. Max gap between shots is ~1.37 s (60f charge + 22f bolt) and ~2.35 s across a reload, both well inside 6 s, so she stays Pierce-tagged after her first shot — which is the correct reading of a per-full-charge 6 s refresh, not an over-model. MBB1 proves it is LIVE (removal reduces total while the 117.64 buff is still applied), which is the exact 'dead pierce block' bug it must discriminate against.

skill1.driverSaid: No primitive for a held-charge trigger or a self-status gate. Mode-split: default 'auto (no Embarrassment)' omits the package entirely (premise: auto-play never holds a completed charge — Prydwen); 'manual (Embarrassment cycle)' approximates it as a permanent operating mode. ⚑1 with a measurement recipe.
skill1.blindSaid: S6: interval sec:12 stand-in, flagged as an UNMEASURED cadence estimate. S2b: GAP, cadence is an ALWAYS-⚑, warns the state duration is nowhere in the prose.
skill1.formulaCheck: The prose gives no Embarrassment state duration and no primitive exists for 'held charge ≥0.5 s' or 'not already in state'. Scope-lock validation is full-auto (mechanics §7), so the default mode is the one the board grades.
skill1.explanation: All three independent derivations agree there is no faithful primitive here; they differ only in the fallback. The driver's mode-split is the most honest of the three for the graded basis (it does not invent a cadence into the validated numbers), but it rests on a COMMUNITY-tier premise no blind agent could see — flagged as gotcha #2 and the owner spot-check.

skill1.driverSaid: flatDamage atkPct 290 flavor 'distributed', enemy target, shotFired trigger — mode 'manual' only, so inert on the default basis
skill1.blindSaid: S5: structural presence PASSES against the driver file (the mode-gated block is still authored); only the behavioral cadence assertion goes RED. S6: same magnitude/flavor on its interval:12 stand-in.
skill1.formulaCheck: Magnitude 290 is the L10 datamined value (description_value_list index 2). Distributed groups with Damage-Taken, not Attack Damage (damage-calculation §1g) — the flavor tag is present and correct here.
skill1.explanation: Encoding is faithful; its ACTIVATION is gated by the mode premise. In manual it fires once per shot, which the collapsed 1-round magazine makes ≈ once per cycle — an approximation the note states outright.

skill1.driverSaid: Passive maxAmmoPct -100 (floors the magazine to 1 → one shot then reload), manual mode only; 'Forced Reload' is implied by the 1-round magazine rather than encoded
skill1.blindSaid: S6 + S2b both chose consumeAmmo{fraction:1}, which is the closer primitive (a per-trigger dump that also fires lastBullet triggers) rather than a permanent capacity cap
skill1.formulaCheck: Reload/ammo lines are damage lines (they gate shots fired — see the reload-speed ruling in memory), so skipping them would be wrong; both encodings honour that. mechanics §11: Max Ammunition ▼ clips the CURRENT belt when it lands.
skill1.explanation: A structural divergence from both blinds, but it only exists inside the non-default manual mode and the driver's note states the approximation and its first-magazine artifact. Two blinds independently preferring consumeAmmo is worth recording for the manual-mode refit, not a defect in the graded basis.

skill1.driverSaid: Passive reloadSpeedPct -50 (manual mode) — explicitly flagged as approximating a reload-COUNT clamp with a permanent additive modifier
skill1.blindSaid: S6: additive -50 for a ⚑ 5 s window; S2b: FIX — must scope to exactly one reload, calls the clamp primitive a known gap
skill1.formulaCheck: mechanics §11: 'reload speed is fixed at x for N rounds' is a stat CLAMP, a different mechanic, still unmodeled; durationShots is explicitly NOT the right primitive for a fixed-at line. Reload is subtractive: displayed × 0.975 × (1−buff) + 13f.
skill1.explanation: All three agree the clamp primitive does not exist. Driver's permanent -50% over-applies in manual (every reload, not just the forced one); documented under ⚑1 with the recipe. Zero effect on the graded auto basis.

skill1.driverSaid: Permanent atkPct 118.7 passive in manual mode (no durationSec), justified as 'refreshed every cycle so effectively always on'; absent in auto
skill1.blindSaid: S5 + S6 + S2b all encode durationSec 40 with per-activation refresh
skill1.formulaCheck: 118.7 is the L10 value; atkPct sums inside (1 + ΣATK%) on staticAtk (damage-calculation §1a) and additively stacks with the burst's 220 — the driver's manual encoding preserves that additivity.
skill1.explanation: The permanent form is a fair approximation only if the cycle is shorter than 40 s, which the driver's collapsed 1-shot cadence guarantees in manual. Divergence from three independent derivations, but confined to the non-graded mode and documented.

skill2.driverSaid: UNMODELED (listed verbatim in override.unmodeled.skill2) — status-gated on Embarrassment, which auto never enters, so inert on the default basis
skill2.blindSaid: S6 models it on the interval stand-in with a ⚑ 5 s window; S2b calls it FIX/status-gated and explicitly asserts it must NOT be live at frame 0
skill2.formulaCheck: DamageUp-bucket Pierce term, live only while she is Pierce-tagged. Correctly inert whenever the Embarrassment state cannot exist.
skill2.explanation: Correct for auto. But manual mode models Embarrassment as PERMANENT while omitting the 64.7% the state grants — an internal inconsistency in that mode (under-credit), recorded as gotcha #3. Documented in the driver's test header ('it WOULD apply in manual mode (a residual there)').

skill2.driverSaid: burstCast → dot atkPct 447.7, intervalSec 2, durationSec 10, enemy target (no flavor field)
skill2.blindSaid: S5 asserts exactly this cadence/magnitude and PASSES on it; S6 authored the identical dot (plus flavor). S2b independently ruled burstCast, NEVER fullBurstEnter, 5 ticks per own cast.
skill2.formulaCheck: 447.7 is the L10 value; the status comes from HER burst, so burstCast keying is the only correct choice — fullBurstEnter would over-fire on the helm-led Full Bursts present in the control comp. Skill-type instance: crits, never cores, no range, FB by landing time (damage-calculation §2b) — the engine routes it to the skill bucket ✓.
skill2.explanation: Cross-family corroborated on trigger, magnitude and cadence. MBB4 pins exactly 5 ticks per full window (discriminating 1-instant and 1 s-interval) and proves no tick follows a helm-led cast. Two residuals attach to this line — the missing distributed flavor (gotcha #4) and the engine's pierce inheritance (gotcha #1) — neither is an encoding error.

burst.driverSaid: UNMODELED (in override.unmodeled.burst); trivially satisfied in auto, where Embarrassment never occurs
burst.blindSaid: S5 skips it as a GAP (no self-status-suppression primitive); S6 calls it 'the single largest known over-credit' of its own single-mode baseline; S2b: MEASUREMENT-GATED, loadBearing false
burst.formulaCheck: No engine primitive suppresses a self kit-state for a window. Purge-vs-block is not stated in the prose, so it is genuinely undeterminable from text.
burst.explanation: Vacuously correct on the graded auto basis. In manual it is a real over-credit (290% procs and an ATK-118.7% refresh can land inside her own burst window) — driver's note states this and states why the counter-buff fix was rejected as a larger error.

burst.blindSaid: S5 asserts self-scope + 10 s + magnitude and PASSES; S6 authored byte-equivalent; S2b: FAITHFUL, burstCast not fullBurstEnter
burst.formulaCheck: DamageUp bucket (damage-calculation §1e), additive with any other Pierce Damage ▲; 117.64 is the L10 value. Only pays out while she is Pierce-tagged, which S1's gainPierce supplies.
burst.explanation: Applied exactly once per her own cast (MBB2 asserts count == her burstCast count, expiry == 600f, targetIdx == her slot, and NO application on the helm-led bursts). Coupled to MBB1 so it is proven live, not a dead buff.

burst.blindSaid: S5 asserts magnitude/self/10 s and additionally proves the window with a 10→40 s counterfactual that must strictly ADD damage — PASSES; S6 identical; S2b: FAITHFUL
burst.formulaCheck: 220 is the L10 value (L1 is 130); atkPct joins (1 + ΣATK%) on staticAtk, inside the DEF subtraction, and stacks additively with 118.7 when both are live.
burst.explanation: Once per own cast, 10 s exactly, self only, never on a helm-led Full Burst; removal collapses her burst-window damage (MBB3). The blind's independent 40 s counterfactual also passed, so the duration is pinned from two directions.

gotchas.summary: The engine's pierceDamagePct applies to ALL of a Pierce-tagged unit's damage, so her 447.7% Distributed rider inherits the burst's +117.64% Pierce Damage — the S2b reviewer reads the kit as Pierce feeding weapon attacks only.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: S2 '...Deals 447.7% of final ATK as Distributed Damage' — the line is never described as Pierce damage. Engine sim.ts:1400 gates on the unit's pierce tag, not the hit's flavor; driver measured 10.96M → 6.70M per tick when gainPierce is removed (~64% of that tick is the Pierce buff). Driver documents this as ⚑2; S6 blind independently reached the OPPOSITE convention ('the two distributed lines are NOT pierce-tagged... if popups show them scaling with Pierce, add pierce:true') and S2b makes rider-inertness a distinguishing assertion.
gotchas.suggestedFix: NEEDS MEASUREMENT — do not change the value. game-mechanics §11's own wording ('benefits any Pierce-damage-type unit') is unit-scoped and therefore consistent with the current engine behavior, so the S2b reading is a hypothesis, not established. Recipe: a milk-blooming-bunny-focus recording; compare a 447.7 Distributed popup inside her burst window (Pierce 117.64 live) against one where her 6 s gainPierce window has lapsed — the ratio distinguishes rider-inherits-Pierce (~1.65×, after removing FB/crit/ATK differences) from rider-exempt (1.00×). Scope note: excluding a rider from the unit's pierce tag would be an engine-core change (per-hit pierce flavor), not an override edit.

gotchas.summary: The whole graded basis rests on one COMMUNITY-tier premise — that full-auto never holds a completed charge 0.5 s, so Embarrassment never fires — which no blind agent could see or corroborate, and her standing COLD kit-status is directionally consistent with the premise being wrong.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: '■ Activates when not in the Embarrassment state and when Full Charge lasts for 0.5 sec or more.' Driver cites Prydwen (game knowledge, not in the kit text) and makes 'auto (no Embarrassment)' the DEFAULT mode; the engine mode gate (sim.ts:663) then filters out the 290% rider, the ATK ▲118.7%, and the whole ammo/reload economy. All three independent derivations (S2b/fable-5, S5, S6) instead assumed the cycle runs, so this premise has ZERO cross-family corroboration. The override's own note records the unit sitting COLD at kit-status 0.56–0.73 (sim below real) — the direction you would expect if real auto-play DOES enter Embarrassment.
gotchas.suggestedFix: NEEDS MEASUREMENT — the mode default is the right call for a full-auto validation basis if the premise holds, and no fudge should be applied either way. Recipe: one scope-lock full-auto recording with milk-blooming-bunny focused, and read two independent observables — (a) any 290%-class Distributed popup (~her staticAtk × 2.9 × buckets), and (b) the ammo counter, which collapses to a 1-round-per-reload cadence under Embarrassment versus her 6-round magazine without it. Either observable settles it alone; both together are decisive. If Embarrassment DOES fire on auto, the default mode must flip and the manual-cycle approximations (⚑1) become load-bearing for the board.

gotchas.summary: Manual mode is internally inconsistent: it models Embarrassment as a PERMANENT state but omits the +64.7% Pierce Damage that state grants, while also ignoring the burst's 10 s immunity that would suspend the cycle.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: S2 '■ Activates only when in Embarrassment status... Pierce Damage ▲ 64.7% continuously.' and burst 'Gains Immunity to Embarrassment for 10 sec.' The driver's manual mode carries the permanent maxAmmoPct -100 / reloadSpeedPct -50 / atkPct 118.7 package, so the unit is by construction always Embarrassed there — yet no pierceDamagePct 64.7 exists anywhere in the file (S6 modeled it; S2b made it load-bearing). The two omissions push opposite ways: -64.7% Pierce is an under-credit, the missing immunity is an over-credit inside her burst window.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Manual mode is not the graded basis, so this changes no board number today. When the ⚑1 manual-play recording lands, rebuild that mode as a real cycle (state entry → 290% + ammo dump + 40 s ATK + 64.7% Pierce for the state's measured duration → immunity blackout across her burst) rather than a permanent operating mode; adding the 64.7% to the current permanent model in isolation would deepen the inconsistency, not fix it.

gotchas.summary: The 447.7% rider is authored as a dot with no flavor field, so it is not tagged 'distributed' — it routes through the sustained/DoT path instead of the Distributed/Taken buckets.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Deals 447.7% of final ATK as Distributed Damage.' damage-calculation §1e/§1g: Distributed groups with Damage-Taken, NOT Attack Damage (an explicit naming trap), and a sustained-flavored instance picks up Sustained Damage ▲. Driver's skill1 flatDamage DOES carry flavor:'distributed', so the omission is a dot-primitive limitation, not an oversight; documented in the override note and re-stated in the test header.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Inert on the control comp as the driver argues (single partless boss, no distributedDamagePct, no Sustained Damage ▲ source), so no change is warranted now. It becomes real in a comp carrying Sustained Damage ▲ or Distributed Damage ▲ — the fix is an engine one (accept flavor on the dot effect), and it should be landed with a board A/B rather than as a silent override edit.

verdictRationale: GO. Every one of the 11 kit lines is either FAITHFUL or a DOCUMENTED_GAP with a stated recipe, and the three load-bearing lines that actually move the graded auto basis — S1's gainPierce 6 s, the burst's self-scoped pierceDamagePct 117.64 / atkPct 220 for 10 s, and S2's burstCast DoT at 447.7% × 2 s × 10 s — are corroborated across families: the cross-family S2b reviewer (fable-5) and both blind opus-5 re-derivations independently reached burstCast (never fullBurstEnter), the same L10 magnitudes, the same 10 s windows, and the same timed-gainPierce-not-static-hasPierce encoding. The driver's tests discriminate rather than decorate: MBB1's counterfactual still APPLIES the 117.64 buff while removing the Pierce tag (so it fails under the old dead-pierce-block bug), MBB2/MBB3 prove own-cast-only against the helm co-B3's Full Bursts that the fixture is asserted to contain, MBB4 pins exactly 5 ticks per window against both 1-instant and 1 s-interval models, and MBB5 pins the mode gate behaviourally in both directions. Convergence is mechanically RED — 8 of the S5 blind's 22 assertions fail — but I traced each one and every failure resolves to the mode split or the deliberately unmodeled 64.7%; none exposes an encoding error, and the blind's own structural check for the 290% rider PASSES because the mode-gated block is still authored in the file, which independently confirms the driver's account of the failure set. Ranked residuals: (1) the engine pierce-tags the 447.7 Distributed rider, worth ~64% of each tick — real, but game-mechanics §11's unit-scoped wording is consistent with the engine, so this is measurement-gated and an engine-core question, not an override fix; (2) the dropped manual-mode 64.7% and the un-flavored dot, both low and both comp-conditional. THE SAME-MODEL RESIDUAL TO SPOT-CHECK IS NOT AN ENCODING AT ALL — it is the premise under the default mode: 'full-auto never holds a completed charge, so Embarrassment never fires' is COMMUNITY-tier game knowledge (Prydwen) invisible to every blind agent, all three of which assumed the cycle runs. Nothing in this gauntlet corroborates it, and the unit's recorded COLD kit-status (0.56–0.73, sim below real) points the same way a wrongly-suppressed Embarrassment package would. One full-auto focus recording settles it from two independent observables — a 290%-class Distributed popup, or her magazine collapsing to one round per reload — and that measurement, not any value change, is the next action.
